annotations.keyFindings: Pre-visit text prompts raised same-day completion from 31 to 62 percent against 29 to 35 percent in comparison clinics; clinicians opened 71 percent of completed scores; older patients and those without smartphones completed less.
annotations.notes: Directly relevant to the prompt option.

annotations.keyFindings: Training plus monthly audit feedback raised completed and discussed measures from 22 to 41 percent against 20 to 24 percent; no difference in six-month response; use fell back after feedback stopped.
annotations.limitations: Variable fidelity; community teams rather than clinics.
annotations.notes: Directly relevant to the training option.

annotations.keyFindings: Measurement-based care was associated with more remission (risk ratio 1.28) across 14 controlled studies, with substantial heterogeneity and varied definitions.
annotations.limitations: Only three community mental health studies; high risk of bias in eight.
annotations.notes: Answers the outcome question only in part.

annotations.keyFindings: Eleven definitions of uptake across 47 studies; only 9 required clinician review of the score; proposes completed and clinician-reviewed at the same visit, per visit, as the core definition.
Patients valued the questionnaire when the score was discussed and stopped completing it when it was ignored.
Treatment changed at 39 percent of non-improving visits with a viewed score against 24 percent with none (odds ratio 1.9).
annotations.limitations: Routinely collected data; outcome effects unknown.
annotations.notes: Supports the causal pathway, not the effect.

annotations.keyFindings: Completion fell from 58 to 39 percent in the year after support ended; clinics with a local champion stayed above 50 percent.
annotations.notes: Durability is a review outcome in its own right.

annotations.keyFindings: Symposium presentations described prompts, dashboards and incentives with increases in completion, without quantitative results.
annotations.limitations: No year, no selection method, no data.
annotations.notes: Quality and certainty cannot be judged from the report.

claims.text: Pre-visit electronic prompts doubled same-day completion of the depression measure in outpatient psychiatry clinics, with little change in comparison clinics.
claims.passage: Completion of the measure on the day of the visit rose from 31 to 62 percent in prompt clinics and from 29 to 35 percent in comparison clinics over nine months.
claims.interpretation: Prompts are a candidate strategy; clinician review must be measured separately.

claims.text: In a cluster randomised trial, training with monthly audit feedback raised completed and discussed measures but did not change six-month response, and use fell back when feedback stopped.
claims.passage: In the six months after feedback stopped, measure use in intervention teams fell back towards baseline.
claims.interpretation: Durability must be a review outcome.

claims.text: Across 14 controlled studies, measurement-based care was associated with a higher chance of depression remission, with substantial heterogeneity.
claims.passage: Measurement-based care was associated with a higher chance of remission (risk ratio 1.28, 95 percent CI 1.07 to 1.53), with substantial heterogeneity.
claims.interpretation: The outcome question has some support but depends on definitions.

claims.text: Only 9 of 47 implementation studies required clinician review of the score when defining uptake.
claims.passage: Only 9 of the 47 studies required that the clinician review the score.
claims.interpretation: The review needs a core uptake definition and must record which definition each study used.

claims.text: Completion fell from 58 to 39 percent in the year after external implementation support ended.
claims.passage: Completion of the measure at depression visits reached 58 percent at the end of support and fell to 39 percent one year later.

synthesis: Eight of 212 retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Electronic prompts and training with feedback both increased measure use in controlled studies, but use fell when support or feedback ended, and the one randomised trial found no change in six-month response. A meta-analysis links measurement-based care to remission with substantial heterogeneity, and uptake is defined in at least eleven ways, so a core definition is needed before any pooling. One conference report could not be assessed.
gradeRationale: One cluster randomised trial, controlled before-after and uncontrolled studies, heterogeneous definitions; only 8 of 212 hits appraised, so this is a scoping judgement for the protocol, not the review's own certainty.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; five claims recorded; one record not assessable; overall certainty low.
